title: SUD Clinical Intake Specialist
description:
Overview

Opportunities Abound at SOUND

SOUND Behavioral Health is growing, and we are welcoming a SUD Clinical Intake Specialist (SUDCIS) to join our team located in Seattle, WA!

The SUD Intake Specialist provides person-centered intake and assessment services for participants seeking substance use disorder treatment at Sound. Responsibilities include conducting assessments for Recovery Helpline referrals, walk-in participants, and other scheduled or assigned intakes based on program and organizational needs. The SUD Intake Specialist partners with participants to identify treatment needs, strengths, recovery goals, and service preferences while facilitating timely access to clinically appropriate care.

The SUD Intake Specialist utilizes ASAM Criteria to support level of care determinations and treatment recommendations and works to promote engagement, reduce barriers to care, and facilitate successful connection to treatment and recovery support services.

Schedule: Monday - Friday between 8:00am - 5:00pm.

Location: In-office at our Capitol Hill Clinic (1600 E Olive Way, Seattle, WA 98122).

Accepting applications until October 5.

Responsibilities

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES

  • Conduct integrated substance use disorder and mental health screenings and assessments to identify treatment needs, strengths, barriers, and recovery goals and to inform treatment recommendations.
  • Conduct comprehensive intake assessments, including psychosocial history, substance use history, co-occurring behavioral health conditions, risk and safety evaluations, and determination of eligibility, medical necessity, and appropriate level of care utilizing ASAM Criteria. Assessments will incorporate collateral information, when clinically indicated and authorized, and will meet all applicable payer, regulatory, accreditation, and organizational documentation requirements.
  • Utilize ASAM Criteria to support level of care determinations, treatment recommendations, and transitions across the continuum of care.
  • Conduct intake assessments for Recovery Helpline referrals, walk-in participants, and other assigned referrals in accordance with program requirements, service demand, and organizational priorities.
  • Promote engagement in treatment by building rapport, addressing barriers to care, coordinating referrals, and supporting participants through the intake and admission process.
  • Facilitate linkage to appropriate treatment, recovery support services, and internal and external community resources based on assessed needs, ASAM level of care recommendations, and participant preferences.
  • Prepare timely and accurate assessments, summaries, reports, progress notes, and related documentation in accordance with agency, regulatory, contractual, and accreditation standards.
  • Participate in multidisciplinary team meetings, individual supervision, and assigned committees as required.
  • Participate in ongoing program development, quality improvement, and utilization review activities.
  • Complete required continuing education and maintain professional competency and applicable credentials.
  • Uphold ethical, professional, and respectful relationships with participants, colleagues, community partners, and referral sources.
  • Apply recovery-oriented, person-centered, culturally responsive, and evidence-based practices consistent with Sound's mission, values, and clinical standards.
  • Comply with all applicable federal, state, county, contractual, and organizational requirements, policies, procedures, and safety standards.
  • Work closely with SUD Program Support Specialists and other internal partners to support timely access to services.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

KEY WORK RELATIONSHIPS

Develops and maintains collaborative working relationships across departments, engaging with team members, management and leadership in a manner that values diverse perspectives and lived experiences. Contributes to a respectful and inclusive work environment by practicing cultural humility, promoting equity in services and decision-making, and supporting efforts that foster a sense of belonging for all.

Other keywords: therapists, therapy, counselors, intakes, counseling, social work, case managers, MSW, MHP, MFT, associate

Qualifications

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Associate’s degree or higher in a related field, or a bachelor’s degree, required for candidates qualifying through the Substance Use Disorder Professional (SUDP) pathway.
  • Minimum of two (2) years of full-time experience in the substance use disorder field required.
  • Experience conducting assessments, applying ASAM Criteria, determining level of care, coordinating referrals, and engaging participants in treatment preferred.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES & REGISTRATIONS

  • Must have a Washington State driver's license and insurable driving record.
  • Must pass a criminal background check.
  • Candidates must meet one of the following qualification pathways:
    • Current Washington State Substance Use Disorder Professional (SUDP) credential; or
    • Have a current active MHP-qualifying credential with DOH (i.e. LICSW, LMHC, LMFT, or an associate- level version of these credentials.

KNOWLEDGE, ABILITIES, AND SKILLS

  • Working knowledge of ASAM Criteria and their application to assessment, level of care determination, treatment recommendations, and care coordination.
  • Knowledge of recovery-oriented practices, motivational interviewing techniques, and engagement strategies that support participation and retention in treatment.
  • Familiarity with substance use disorder treatment systems, recovery support services, and community referral resources.
  • Familiarity working with legally involved participants and understanding court, probation, and recovery support requirements.
  • Knowledge of behavioral health resources, healthcare delivery systems, funding mechanisms, and applicable clinical service requirements.
  • Ability to quickly establish rapport and effectively engage participants seeking substance use disorder treatment.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while responding effectively to urgent or crisis situations.
  • Strong computer, keyboarding, documentation, and electronic health record skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with participants from diverse backgrounds with professionalism, respect, and cultural humility.

SENSORY/PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS

The requirement described below are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Sensory:

  • Communicate effectively with clients, colleagues, and community partners in person, by telephone, and through virtual platforms.
  • Hear and understand conversations in person and over the phone in office and community SUD Clinical Intake Specialist settings.
  • Read and interpret written materials, clinical documentation, policies, and electronic health records.
  • Observe and assess client behavior, emotional state, and environmental safety cues during clinical interactions.

title: Systems Engineer II
description:
Who will you be working with?

Wabtec's Train Handling solutions include Trip Optimizer® and Locotrol®, which work together to optimize train performance and automate freight operations. Trip Optimizer creates and executes fuel-efficient operating plans that meet schedule and train-handling requirements, while Locotrol enables coordinated control of distributed locomotives throughout the train. Together, these technologies improve train handling, fuel efficiency, operational safety, and the ability to operate longer and heavier trains.

As a Systems Engineer, you will work closely with engineering teams, product management, and railroad customers to support the development of innovative solutions that advance automation within the rail industry.

How will you make a difference?

As a Systems Engineer, you will support the design, development, testing, and deployment of Wabtec's Train Handling portfolio. Working under the guidance of experienced engineers, you will contribute to requirements development, system analysis, verification activities, and product enhancements while adhering to established engineering processes and standards.

The successful candidate will demonstrate an AI-enabled mindset, leveraging AI tools to improve research, problem-solving, productivity, and technical decision-making. You will continuously learn emerging technologies and apply data-driven insights to help deliver high-quality solutions that meet customer and business needs.

What do we want to know about you?

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Mathematics or Computer Science from an accredited college or university
  • Minimum of 1-2 years hands-on design, requirements development and implementation experience involving; Engineering Systems, Hardware / Software Engineering, and/or Data Information Systems
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Strong oral and written communication skills
  • Ability to work in a cross-functional, global environment
  • Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally

What will your typical day look like?

  • Support the design, development, testing, and enhancement of Train Handling solutions while applying sound engineering principles and established development processes.
  • Assist in gathering, documenting, and analyzing customer and system requirements to support product development and continuous improvement activities.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including Product Management, Software Engineering, Train Control, Office Systems, Safety, Validation, and Applications Engineering, to support project execution and successful product delivery.
  • Participate in requirements reviews, design reviews, verification activities, and technical discussions throughout the product development lifecycle.
  • Assist in troubleshooting technical issues, analyzing system behavior, and supporting resolution efforts under the guidance of senior engineers.
  • Contribute to field testing, validation, and evaluation activities for train automation and optimization solutions.
  • Support the preparation of technical documentation, reports, project updates, and engineering deliverables.
  • Work with railroad subject matter experts and engineering teams to learn operational concepts and apply them to product development efforts.
  • Develop knowledge of industry standards, engineering best practices, and emerging technologies relevant to train automation, optimization, and distributed control systems.
  • Utilize AI-enabled tools and technologies to improve productivity, accelerate learning, support analysis activities, and enhance engineering outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Foundational understanding of systems engineering principles and product development processes.
  • Exposure to software, controls, automation, transportation, or embedded systems through coursework, internships, or project experience.
  • Familiarity with systems architecture concepts and distributed systems is a plus.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Interest in applying AI-enabled tools and data-driven approaches to engineering challenges.
  • Knowledge of railroad operations, AAR standards, CENELEC standards, or safety-critical systems is preferred but not required.

Relocation assistance may be provided if eligibility requirements are met.

Wabtec will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the U.S. for this opening. Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen (as applicable) and fitness for duty test (as applicable).

What could you accomplish in a place that puts People First?

At Wabtec, it’s not just about a job - it’s about the impact you make. When our people come together, we’re Expanding the Possible by continuously improving what we do and how we do it - for our clients and each other.

If you’re ready to revolutionize how the world moves for future generations, Wabtec is the place for you.

title: Senior IT Systems & Network Engineer
description:
Why This Role Exists

Lyte is building perception systems that combine custom silicon, sensors, and software for robotics, mobility, and next-generation automation. As the company grows, its internal technology environment must become more secure, reliable, scalable, and cost-effective without adding unnecessary complexity.

This role will help turn a growing IT environment into a well-controlled, supportable operation. You will work directly across identity, endpoints, Linux systems, cloud infrastructure, networking, security, vendors, and compliance. This is a hands-on individual contributor role for someone who can identify a problem, make a sound technical decision, and carry the solution through implementation.

What you'll Accomplish

  • In your first 30 days, you will complete knowledge transfer across Lyte’s core IT systems, operating practices, vendors, and active projects. You will begin independently resolving recurring issues and establish working relationships with Engineering and other key partners.
  • Within your first 90 days, you will take ownership of assigned systems and deliver a meaningful milestone on a priority initiative, such as the Jamf MDM rollout, identity and endpoint improvements, and infrastructure setup for new offices and sites.
  • Within six months, you will strengthen the company’s identity and endpoint security by improving controls across Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Intune, Jamf, MFA, Conditional Access, RBAC, encryption, patching, EDR, and vulnerability remediation.
  • You will improve infrastructure reliability and supportability across Linux systems, firewalls, office networks, VPN access, cloud services, storage, backups, and business-continuity capabilities. Improvements will be documented and measured against priorities agreed with the IT leadership team.
  • You will reduce avoidable cost and manual work by improving visibility into cloud, SaaS, licensing, compute, and storage spend and by automating high-value IT and security workflows using Bash, PowerShell, Python, or similar tools.
  • By the end of your first year, the systems you own should be more secure, better documented, easier to operate, and less dependent on individual knowledge. You will have helped reduce priority risks, improve audit readiness, and give the company a stronger foundation for continued growth.

What We Need

  • Demonstrated ownership of Microsoft 365, Entra ID, and Intune environments, including identity lifecycle management, MFA, Conditional Access, RBAC, Exchange, SharePoint, or Teams
  • Hands-on administration and troubleshooting of Linux systems, including hardening, patching, access controls, monitoring, and availability
  • Experience configuring and supporting enterprise networking, firewalls, segmentation, switching, VPNs, and remote access
  • Ownership of mixed macOS, Windows, or Linux endpoint environments using platforms such as Intune, Jamf, EDR, encryption, and vulnerability-management tools
  • Evidence of independently delivering infrastructure or security projects from problem identification through implementation, documentation, and operational handoff
  • Working automation experience with Bash, PowerShell, Python, or a comparable scripting language

This is a senior role requiring broad, hands-on depth, typically developed over 12 or more years. We will place the greatest weight on the scale of the environments you have owned, the decisions you made, and the results you delivered.

Preferred, but Not Required

  • Experience with AWS, Azure, or GCP; SOC 2 or ISO 27001; SIEM and logging platforms; GitLab or CI/CD environments; AI-tool governance; GPU or AI/ML infrastructure; EDA or EPDA environments; and technology-vendor or licensing negotiations. Equivalent platforms and adjacent technical experience are welcome.

How You’ll Work

  • Lyte is a hands-on, highly technical environment where people are expected to take ownership and move quickly from identifying a problem to implementing a solution. The IT team is lean, so you will work across operations, infrastructure, security, and active company projects rather than staying within a narrow specialty.
  • You will partner closely with Engineering and other technical teams, and your work will have direct visibility and impact as the company grows. This role is best suited to someone who is comfortable with changing priorities, enjoys solving unfamiliar problems, and wants the opportunity to build and improve systems rather than simply maintain them.
  • This individual contributor role is based in Lyte’s Sunnyvale office five days per week and may occasionally require evening or weekend work for maintenance, deployments, or urgent incidents.

Benefits (subject to location and local regulations)

  • Competitive salary and equity
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Flexible vacation and time-off policy
  • Collaborative, fast-paced, and inclusive work environment
  • Opportunity to work on cutting-edge technologies with a highly cross-functional team

title: Data Engineer
description:
Job Description

Purpose of the role Build and maintain all data pipelines feeding the Databricks lakehouse, ensuring clean, timely, and governed data flows from every source across the Investment Division’s five portfolio clusters and, in later phases, the Group’s operating divisions. Own the bronze-to-silver-to-gold transformation logic, data quality monitoring, security master management, and the Document Intelligence Engine’s ingestion and classification pipelines. Key responsibilities Build and maintain automated ingestion pipelines: Addepar API (daily positions, transactions, cash), Capital IQ API (prices, fundamentals, consensus), Canoe (alternative fund documents), eVestment/Mercer (manager database), email (Outlook Graph API). Implement the medallion architecture: bronze layer (raw immutable data), silver layer (cleaned, conformed, security master mapped, FX normalised, GICS classified, entity ownership resolved), gold layer (analytics-ready tables optimised for ML and SQL queries). Build and maintain the security master: mapping ISIN, CUSIP, SEDOL, Bloomberg ticker, and custodian internal identifiers across all sources, handling corporate actions (mergers, ticker changes, share class conversions). Build the data quality monitoring framework: automated checks for completeness, timeliness, and reconciliation, with exception alerts to the operations analyst. Build the Document Intelligence Engine ingestion pipeline: receive documents from email, file drop, and Canoe; route to the classification and extraction models (built by the ML engineer); store structured output in gold layer tables and raw text in the vector store. Build the reverse pipeline: push model outputs (factor scores, anomaly flags, risk metrics) from the lakehouse to Addepar via API as custom position attributes. In later phases, build ingestion pipelines for operating division ERP systems (Nama core banking, UMG DMS, hotel PMS, IFM CMMS, electronics POS). Monitor pipeline health daily: investigate and resolve ingestion failures, data quality alerts, and schema changes from upstream sources. Optimise pipeline performance and cost: right-size compute clusters, implement incremental processing, manage storage lifecycle. Qualifications and experience 5–8 years of data engineering experience, with at least 2 years on Databricks or equivalent Spark-based platforms. Strong proficiency in Python, SQL, PySpark, and Delta Live Tables. Experience building API integrations and working with financial data feeds (custodian files, market data APIs, fund administrator reports). Understanding of security master management and corporate action processing in financial services. Experience with Azure Data Factory, Azure Blob Storage, and Azure Functions. Familiarity with document processing pipelines (PDF parsing, OCR, text extraction). Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or equivalent. Detail-oriented with strong debugging and problem-solving skills.

description:
The Entwistle Company is seeking a skilled and motivated Quality Assurance Specialist to build a long-term career in our collaborative and innovative environment.

In this role, you’ll help deliver mission-critical components that support U.S. and allied defense, with your skills, creativity, and impact directly contributing to national and global security. We value talent, encourage innovation, and promote professional growth.

The Quality Assurance Specialist owns the coordination, investigation, and timely closure of customer, DCMA, and internal corrective actions. This position addresses a critical business risk by preventing unresolved findings and corrective actions from delaying manufacturing activities. The role works across Quality, Engineering, Operations, Purchasing, Contracts, and Program Management to identify root causes, implement sustainable corrective actions, and verify effectiveness


Ready to make a real difference? Join us.


Our Mission Statement

  1. To be an essential provider of mission-critical defense components & systems, spanning air, land, sea and space, recognized for our specialized capabilities, quality and dependability.
  2. To design, manufacture & build-to-print innovative and cost-effective products.
  3. To help our DoD, Prime and Foreign Military customers and US warfighter succeed in their missions.

At The Entwistle Company, our values—Trust, Respect, Accountability, Collaboration, and Commitment—guide everything we do, from daily decisions to long-term strategy.


Key Responsibilities:

· Own customer and Defense Contract Management Agency corrective action requests from initial receipt through approved closure.

· Lead or facilitate structured root cause investigations using appropriate methods such as 5 Why, fishbone analysis, fault tree analysis, or 8D.

· Coordinate corrective action assignments, due dates, supporting evidence, and cross functional follow through.

· Evaluate proposed corrective actions for adequacy and verify implementation and effectiveness before recommending or approving closure within delegated authority.

· Identify recurring or systemic issues and escalate them to the Quality Systems and Process Specialist and Quality leadership for broader process improvement.

· Conduct internal quality system and process audits with emphasis on corrective action compliance and effectiveness.

· Issue audit findings, initiate corrective actions, place affected work or material on hold, and require containment when authorized by the Quality Management System.

· Support development and revision of procedures and processes related to nonconformance, corrective action, and audit response.

· Maintain accurate corrective action logs, status reports, objective evidence, and closure records.

· Analyze corrective action, aging recurrence, and closure performance and communicate risks, priorities, and overdue actions to responsible leaders.

· Support customer source inspection and regulatory review activities related to findings and corrective actions.

· Perform other related duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

· Bachelor’s degree in engineering, quality, manufacturing or a related field or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience.

· Three to five years of quality assurance corrective action auditing or manufacturing quality experience in a regulated manufacturing environment.

· Demonstrated experience leading root cause investigations and corrective action implementation.

· Working knowledge of quality management systems, technical procedures, drawings specifications, and government or customer requirements.

· Ability to manage multiple corrective actions and drive timely follow through across departments.

· Strong written communication, documentation, facilitation, and problem-solving skills.

· Proficiency with Microsoft Office and quality or enterprise systems used to track findings actions and records.

title: Data Modeller
description:
Salary: AUD 1100 - 1300 per day

Data Modeller| 12-Month Contract | Brisbane Based candidates

Join a major enterprise data transformation initiative, helping shape trusted, business-ready data products within a modern Databricks Lakehouse environment. This is an opportunity for an experienced Data Modeller who enjoys working closely with business stakeholders and technical teams to define, validate, and design logical datasets that drive reporting, analytics, and data-led decision-making.

The Opportunity

Our client's Enterprise Data Group has established a modern Lakehouse platform and continues to expand its enterprise analytics capabilities. As a Data Modeller, you will play a critical role in translating business requirements into logical data structures that support reporting and analytical outcomes across multiple business domains.

This is not a Data Engineering position. We are seeking a dedicated Data Modeller who can bridge business and technical teams, establish common data definitions, and guide the design of scalable, reusable data assets.

Key Responsibilities
  • Collaborate with Business Stakeholders, Business Analysts, Architects, Data Owners and Data Engineers to understand business requirements and analytical use cases.
  • Design and maintain logical data models and business-focused datasets.
  • Facilitate workshops to define business concepts, entities, attributes and measures.
  • Identify authoritative data sources and establish agreed business definitions.
  • Analyse source systems and existing Lakehouse data assets to understand relationships and business meaning.
  • Develop and maintain data dictionaries, business glossaries and metadata assets.
  • Validate and refine datasets through iterative prototyping and stakeholder engagement.
  • Ensure alignment with enterprise data governance, architecture and security standards.
  • Partner closely with Data Engineers to support implementation of agreed designs within the Lakehouse environment.
About You

You are a modern, pragmatic Data Modeller who thrives in agile delivery environments and can balance modelling rigour with delivery speed. You are comfortable moving from business requirements to implementation-ready designs while building strong relationships with a broad range of stakeholders.

Essential:
  • 5+ years' experience in Data Modelling, Data Warehousing, Analytics Engineering or similar roles.
  • Proven experience translating business requirements into logical data models and analytical datasets.
  • Strong understanding of dimensional modelling and modern data modelling techniques.
  • Experience analysing complex source systems and data structures.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement, workshop facilitation and communication skills.
  • Experience documenting business definitions, data mappings and metadata.
  • Understanding of data governance, data quality and authoritative source concepts.
  • Experience working in agile delivery environments.
Highly Desirable:
  • Experience with Databricks and modern Lakehouse architectures.
  • Experience working with Enterprise Data Models or Information Models.
  • Background within Energy, Utilities or similar asset-intensive environments.
  • Exposure to cloud-based analytics platforms and data product development.
What's on Offer?
  • Initial 12-month contract with potential extensions.
  • Brisbane-based engagement with a leading Queensland organisation.
  • Opportunity to work on enterprise-scale analytics and data transformation initiatives.
  • Collaborative environment with modern cloud and data technologies.
  • High-impact role influencing strategic reporting and data-driven decision making.
Apply Now If you're a Data Modeller who enjoys working at the intersection of business and data, and you're passionate about designing modern analytical datasets within a Databricks Lakehouse environment, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Director of Customer Services Center
description:
Introduction

Since 1973, East West Bank has served as a pathway to success. With over 110 locations across the U.S. and Asia, we are the premier financial bridge between the East and West. Our teams of experienced, multi-cultural professionals help guide businesses and community members on both sides of the Pacific looking to explore new markets and create new opportunities, and our sustained growth and expertise in industries like real estate, entertainment and media, private equity and venture capital, and high-tech help build sustainable businesses and expand our associates’ potential for career advancement.

Headquartered in California, East West Bank (Nasdaq: EWBC) is a top-performing commercial bank with a strong foundation, an enterprising spirit and a commitment to absolute integrity. East West Bank gives people the confidence to reach further.

Overview

East West Bank is currently seeking a Director of Customer Service Center (CSC) to lead the Bank’s enterprise customer service center operations and support exceptional customer and branch service experience.

Reporting to the Managing Director, Head of Banking Operations, this leader will be responsible for driving operational excellence, service quality, workforce effectiveness, risk management, issue resolution, and process improvement across the Customer Service Centers. The Director will partner closely with Retail Banking, Branch Operations, Deposit Operations, Loan Operations, Compliance, BSA, Legal, Technology, Digital Banking Operations, and other business partners to enhance service delivery, strengthen controls, improve escalation management, and support the Bank’s continued growth. This role requires a strong people leader with deep call center and banking operations experience, a customer-first mindset, and the ability to execute strategic initiatives in a fast-paced, regulated environment.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute strategic plans to elevate the Bank’s customer service capabilities, service standards, and customer experience across the Customer Service Centers.
  • Build, standardize, and enforce consistent customer service levels, operating procedures, escalation protocols, call quality expectations, and service behaviors across all call units, including internal teams and contracted staff supporting the Bank’s customer service functions.
  • Lead ongoing process improvement initiatives to streamline workflows, improve operational efficiency, improve response times, enhance quality assurance, strengthen controls, and create a more consistent service experience for customers, branches, and internal business partners.
  • Identify operational gaps, service bottlenecks, recurring customer issues, and escalation trends; perform root-cause analysis and partner with business, operations, risk, compliance, and technology teams to implement sustainable corrective actions.
  • Develop and execute talent acquisition and workforce development strategies to attract, retain, and grow multilingual call agents with English, Chinese, and Spanish language capabilities to support the Bank’s diverse customer base.
  • Develop and execute strategies to reduce staff turnover and promote clear growth paths by strengthening associate engagement, manager effectiveness, onboarding, training quality, career development, recognition, retention programs, readiness criteria, succession planning, and promotion opportunities for all levels of associates.
  • Oversee and coordinate service expectations for contracted VXI staff supporting customers in Greater China areas, ensuring alignment with East West Bank’s service standards, compliance requirements, quality expectations, escalation handling, and customer experience objectives.
  • Develop, cascade, and monitor SMART goals for all levels of associates, including managers, supervisors, team leads, and frontline service representatives, ensuring goals are specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound.
  • Align individual, team, and department goals with the Bank’s broader priorities, including service quality, operational efficiency, first-call resolution, customer satisfaction, risk management, compliance adherence, and employee development.
  • Define, track, and report CSC key performance indicators and key risk indicators, including service level performance, call volume trends, average speed of answer, abandonment rate, first-call resolution, quality assurance scores, complaints, escalations, error rates, aging items, and compliance-related metrics.
  • Establish regular performance review routines, dashboards, and management reports to monitor productivity, service quality, risk exposure, staffing effectiveness, associate turnover, language coverage, service consistency, and progress against goals; use data and trends to drive accountability and timely management action.
  • Provide coaching and performance feedback to leaders and associates based on KPI and KRI results, customer feedback, quality reviews, audit findings, staffing trends, turnover indicators, and operational performance.
  • Promote a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, ownership, collaboration, customer-focused execution, associate growth, and consistent service delivery across the Customer Service Centers.
  • Other responsibilities may be assigned

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field preferred.
  • Minimum 10 years of customer service center, call center, banking operations, branch operations, deposit operations, or related financial services experience.
  • Minimum 5 years of management or leadership experience, including leading teams in a high-volume service or operations environment.
  • Strong operational, analytical, workforce management, and process improvement skills.
  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, manage change, and drive measurable results.
  • Strong project management, organizational, issue resolution, and problem-solving abilities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present effectively to senior leadership and business partners.
  • Ability to effectively interact with all levels of the organization and build trusted partnerships across business, operations, risk, compliance, and technology teams.
  • Knowledge of banking regulations, operational controls, customer service risk management, audit expectations, and compliance requirements.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, competing deadlines, and complex operational issues in a fast-paced environment.
  • High level of professionalism, initiative, sound judgment, ownership, and sense of urgency.

Applicants must have legal authorization to work in the United States. We do not offer visa sponsorship at this time.

The base pay range for this position is USD $140,000.00/Yr. - USD $200,000.00/Yr. Exact offers will be determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and location.

description:
Overview

As a patient-focused organization, University of Utah Health exists to enhance the health and well-being of people through patient care, research and education. University of Utah Health seeks staff that are committed to the values of compassion, collaboration, innovation, responsibility, integrity, quality and trust that are integral to our mission. EO/AA

Performs duties to assist the Medical Physicist in performing external beam machine quality assurance (QA) and brachytherapy procedures and QA, patient specific QA, protocol management and implementation of new procedures.

Corporate Overview: The University of Utah is a Level 1 Trauma Center and is nationally ranked and recognized for our academic research, quality standards and overall patient experience. Our five hospitals and eleven clinics provide excellence in our comprehensive services, medical advancement, and overall patient outcomes.

Responsibilities

Essential Functions

External beam machine QA
  • Assists/performs weekly, monthly and annual QA for linear accelerators (linac) and CT, participates in evaluation of the results and reports to the physicists with any concerns.
  • May assist in performing proton morning QA.
  • Ensures that machine QA is performed in a timely manner.
Brachytherapy procedures and QA
  • Assists the brachytherapy physicist team to ensure safe and smooth treatment delivery with Prostate Seed Implants, Eye Plaque Implants and High Dose Rate Brachytherapy.
  • Coordinates PSI seed ordering process, including source delivering and on-site seed QA, inventory, and radiation safety documentation/communication with the campus health physicists.
  • Communicates with the Qualified Medical Physicist (QMP) and the rest of the team including the physician and nurse when potential issues, such as seed order/delivery schedule and QA discrepancy, arise.
  • Assists PSI procedures in the operating room. Under the supervision of the QMP, ensures the sources are all accounted for before and after the PSI procedure.
Oversight and Maintenance of QA Equipment
  • Maintains QA equipment inventory, and ensures that appropriate calibration is performed for each QA device.
  • Facilitates damaged and/or defective QA equipment replacement and repair process.
  • Assists in the maintenance of clinical treatment equipment including quality control (QC) and storage process. For example, stereotactic radiosurgery frame and hardware cleaning, inventory/storage, and QC.
  • Participates in intradepartmental educational sessions and meetings that pertain to hardware QA/QC.
Patient Specific QA
  • Performs patient specific QA for IMRT photon plans.
  • Performs initial troubleshooting when QA fails. Responsible for bringing potential issue/s to the physicist's attention for additional analysis and corrective action.
  • Assists or performs independent proton specific patient QA.
Protocol Management
  • Prepares required protocol documents for submission.
  • Ensures that credentialing requirements have been met for clinical protocols.
  • Attends meetings, refines workflows, maintains and files credentialing letters and responds to other requests from the Clinical Trials Office (CTO).
Implementation of New Procedures
  • Assists the Medical Physicist in implementation of new processes or procedures, programs or workflow in the clinic such as establishment of a new QA platform, creation of source calibration for a new brachytherapy program etc.

Knowledge / Skills / Abilities

  • Demonstrated attention to detail and strong analytical skills.
  • Ability to perform detailed measurements using modern, sensitive instrumentation.
  • Demonstrates ability to work independently as well as in a team environment.
  • Demonstrates ability to provide clear and professional written/verbal communication.
  • Demonstrates accountability for work, taking ownership for quality and timeliness of work.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's or higher degree (physical sciences preferred) from an accredited college or university and/or certification as a Radiation Therapist, or the equivalency.

Qualifications (Preferred)

Working Conditions and Physical Demands

Employee must be able to meet the following requirements with or without an accommodation.

Carrying, Climbing, Color Determination, Crawling, Far Vision, Lifting, Listening, Manual Dexterity, Near Vision, Pulling and/or Pushing, Reaching, Sitting, Speaking, Standing, Stooping and Crouching, Tasting or Smelling, Walking

Television Unscripted Business & Legal Affairs team, supporting one of the industry's leading producers of unscripted programming across broadcast, cable, streaming, and emerging media platforms. This role requires substantial experience structuring and negotiating complex business arrangements and independently managing a wide range of transactional matters. You will negotiate, draft, and analyze development, production, and distribution agreements while providing practical, business-oriented legal advice that supports both creative and commercial priorities. The ideal candidate will possess strong analytical skills, exceptional attention to detail, and the ability to balance competing priorities while delivering effective legal solutions.


As Director, Legal, you will serve as a trusted advisor to the Warner Bros. Television Unscripted Business & Legal Affairs organization, working closely with internal stakeholders and external partners to facilitate the creation, production, and distribution of unscripted content. You will negotiate business and legal terms, advise on contractual matters, and collaborate with creative executives, production teams, and talent representatives to support programming across multiple platforms and distribution models.


Success in this role requires the ability to operate independently while managing a high volume of work in a fast-paced production environment. The ideal candidate will be resourceful, organized, and proactive, with strong judgment and excellent communication skills. The ability to build strong working relationships across business, creative, and legal functions, while effectively navigating complex negotiations and evolving business needs, is essential.


As a member of the Unscripted Legal team, you will help support a broad range of content initiatives spanning traditional and emerging media platforms. You will play a critical role in enabling the successful development and production of programming while ensuring legal and business considerations are thoughtfully addressed throughout the content lifecycle.


This role offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of entertainment, production, and business strategy while supporting a globally recognized portfolio of unscripted programming. You will collaborate with industry-leading creative and business teams and contribute to the continued success and growth of Warner Bros. Television's unscripted content business.


Your Role Accountabilities


  • Negotiate and draft agreements in connection with all aspects of content development, production, and distribution, including but not limited to network licensing agreements, rights agreements, shopping agreements, above-the-line talent agreements (e.g., producers, on-screen talent), options, purchase agreements, format deals, production services agreements, contestant and participant agreements, releases, trade out and branded partnership agreements, contingent compensation definitions, composer agreements, music licenses, and location agreements.
  • Provide legal advice to company and production personnel on all matters relating to the production, distribution and marketing of original content. This includes, but is not limited to, advising on union and nonunion guild obligations, researching and providing legal advice for filming in the U.S. and internationally, clearing content, rights research, providing general production legal support, advising on marketing and advertising restrictions, and negotiating with networks/licensees.
  • Ensure compliance with Warner Bros. Discovery and corporate legal policies and practices, as well as applicable laws and regulations; provide risk assessments to senior business and legal executives; engage and supervise outside counsel, clearance coordinator, and outside music licensing services.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.


Qualifications & Experience


  • 7+ years of practicing law with a national law firm, a major film or television studio, or major online service or platform preferred.
  • BA/BS degree required.
  • Juris Doctorate degree.
  • Must be a CA state bar member and bar membership must be in good standing.
  • Must have knowledge of law and legal environment of entertainment industry sufficient to draft and negotiate legal documents and counsel management on legal implications of their actions.
  • Must be able to analyze, draft and negotiate contracts.
  • Must be able to research legal questions and communicate responses effectively to all levels of corporate and production staff.
  • Must be able to write in a well-organized, concise and precise manner.
  • Must be able to supervise paralegal and clerical subordinates engaged in performance of legal-related tasks.
  • Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Ability to build strong internal client relationships with personnel of all levels, effectively advise senior-level executives, and produce strong client and partner satisfaction through practical and strategic thinking.
  • Must be agile, proactive, and highly motivated; must have positive, team-oriented attitude, excellent judgment, ability to handle high volume of work with minimal supervision and to assess risk, make decisions and prioritize multiple projects with competing deadlines.

description:
Job Description

Job Description: Data Governance Engineer

Location: Mahindra Research Valley (MRV), Chennai

Experience: 5 to 8 Years

Role Summary

We are seeking a highly motivated Data Governance Engineer to establish, implement, and sustain enterprise-wide data governance frameworks across business and engineering functions. The role will focus on improving data quality, metadata management, data lineage, security, compliance, and governance automation to enable trusted and reliable data-driven decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

Data Governance Framework

  • Define and implement data governance policies, standards, processes, and controls across the data lifecycle.
  • Establish governance operating models, roles, responsibilities, and accountability structures.
  • Collaborate with business and technology stakeholders to enforce governance practices.

Data Quality Management

  • Define data quality standards, KPIs, and monitoring mechanisms.
  • Drive data quality improvement initiatives and remediation programs.
  • Work with data owners and stewards to ensure consistent data quality across domains.

Metadata & Data Catalog Management

  • Implement and maintain enterprise metadata repositories and data catalog solutions.
  • Establish data lineage and traceability across source systems, data platforms, and reporting layers.
  • Ensure accurate documentation and classification of enterprise data assets.

Data Security & Compliance

  • Define data classification frameworks and access control mechanisms.
  • Ensure compliance with organizational, regulatory, and privacy requirements.
  • Support secure data sharing and retention policies.

Data Product Governance

  • Define governance standards for data products covering ownership, quality, lineage, usability, and security.
  • Establish certification and review processes for business-critical data products.

Governance Technology & Automation

  • Implement governance controls within data platforms and engineering solutions.
  • Drive automation of governance processes using modern data governance tools.
  • Monitor governance adoption and compliance through dashboards and reporting.

Required Skills

  • Strong understanding of Data Governance, Data Management, and Data Quality frameworks.
  • Hands-on experience with Metadata Management and Data Catalog tools (Collibra, Alation, Microsoft Purview, Informatica, etc.).
  • Knowledge of Data Lineage, Master Data Management (MDM), and Data Stewardship concepts.
  • Experience in Data Security, Privacy, Access Management, and Compliance.
  • Familiarity with Cloud Data Platforms (Azure, AWS, or GCP).
  • Strong SQL and data analysis skills.
  • Experience in governance implementation within large-scale enterprise environments.

Preferred Qualifications

title: Senior Director, Solutions Architecture
description:
Responsibilities

We are seeking a Lead Solution Architect (LSA) to lead the development of differentiated, technically credible, and executable solutions for complex Federal Government opportunities. This is a Senior Director-level leadership role for a technology executive who can connect customer mission needs, enterprise architecture, modernization strategy, delivery execution, and business growth.

The LSA will serve as a senior technical and strategic advisor throughout the opportunity lifecycle—working closely with Capture, Business Development, Program Leadership, Engineering, Pricing, and executive stakeholders to translate customer requirements into compelling solutions designed to perform against evaluation criteria and deliver measurable customer outcomes.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience leading large-scale Federal technology programs, enterprise modernization, cloud solutions, software engineering organizations, and competitive business development efforts, with the executive presence to engage directly with senior government customers and internal leadership.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead end-to-end solution development for complex Federal Government opportunities, from customer requirements and solution strategy through proposal submission and transition to execution.
  • Establish the technical and architectural vision for solutions spanning enterprise applications, cloud modernization, software development, systems integration, data, AI-enabled capabilities, and digital transformation.
  • Lead multidisciplinary Solution Teams and direct technical, engineering, architecture, and subject matter expert contributions to develop a cohesive solution.
  • Translate customer mission needs, requirements, and proposal evaluation criteria into a compliant, differentiated, and executable technical approach.
  • Partner with Capture and Business Development leadership to shape win strategies, solution discriminators, pricing approaches, and customer engagement strategies.
  • Develop and articulate solution strengths, technical discriminators, modernization approaches, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Engage directly with senior government executives, contracting officers, and customer stakeholders to understand priorities, shape requirements, and position solutions for long-term program success.
  • Ensure proposed solutions are operationally executable by considering architecture, delivery model, staffing, technology, cost, schedule, risk, governance, and transition requirements.
  • Lead solution reviews and executive-level technical presentations, translating complex technology concepts into clear business and mission outcomes.
  • Provide technical leadership across RFI/RFP responses, white papers, demonstrations, prototypes, customer briefings, and other business development activities.
  • Apply emerging technologies—including Generative AI, cloud, automation, analytics, and modern software engineering practices—where they create meaningful customer and business value.
  • Develop reusable solution approaches, architectures, collateral, and methodologies that strengthen the organization's broader capture and delivery capabilities.
  • Serve as a senior technical advisor to executive leadership on technology strategy, investment priorities, customer needs, solution risk, and growth opportunities.

Leadership Scope

This role will operate at the intersection of technology, customer strategy, delivery, and growth. The successful candidate will be expected to influence across organizational boundaries, lead senior technical professionals, and establish credibility with both government executives and internal business leaders.

The role requires someone who can move comfortably from executive strategy to architectural detail, while maintaining focus on customer outcomes, competitive differentiation, and successful program execution.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • 18+ years of progressive experience in technology leadership, enterprise architecture, solution development, program management, software engineering, or related disciplines.
  • Demonstrated experience leading large-scale Federal Government technology programs and modernization initiatives.
  • Proven experience developing and presenting technical solutions for RFI/RFP and competitive business development opportunities.
  • Strong experience with enterprise architecture, cloud modernization, software development, systems integration, and digital transformation.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead large, multidisciplinary technical and program organizations.
  • Experience translating complex customer requirements into compliant, differentiated, and executable solutions.
  • Demonstrated experience partnering with Business Development and Capture organizations on solution strategy, proposal development, pricing, and customer engagement.
  • Strong understanding of the relationship between customer requirements, evaluation criteria, technical solution, pricing, staffing, delivery, and contract execution.
  • Experience engaging directly with senior Federal Government executives, contracting officers, and customer stakeholders.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical strategies and architectures to both technical and executive audiences.
  • Demonstrated business acumen, including experience with budgets, financial modeling, pricing, P&L, or business growth.
  • Experience leading organizational transformation and building high-performing, geographically distributed teams.
  • Strong executive presence, written communication, presentation, facilitation, and relationship-building skills.
  • U.S. Citizenship

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, Business, or a related discipline.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance.
  • Experience supporting DoD, VA, DLA, MHS, or other major Federal agencies.
  • Experience with FedRAMP-authorized cloud environments and Federal SaaS solutions.
  • Experience with Generative AI, AI-enabled solutions, automation, analytics, or modern application development.
  • Experience developing prototypes, demonstrations, solution collateral, or reusable architectures for capture activities.
  • Experience managing programs or organizations exceeding $100M in annual value and/or teams of 100+ professionals.
  • Experience with major ERP/HCM modernization, enterprise applications, or large-scale systems integration.

title: IndieWire: Film and Media Reporter
description:
IndieWire: Film and Media Reporter

IndieWire is seeking a dynamic Film and Media Reporter for its Los Angeles office reporting to the Editor-in-Chief. This is a growth role — a deliberate expansion in responsibility and editorial reach — and we're looking for a journalist who brings energy, curiosity, and ambition to one of the most exciting beats in entertainment media. You'll cover the full spectrum: independent filmmakers, actors, craftspeople, and indie distributors alongside major studios and the largest media companies in the world.

We're the voice of creative independence, and you should have a working knowledge of what that means — how independent film and other content has evolved in tandem with the marketplace. This isn't a job built on press junkets and glossy features; it's an opportunity to investigate the film industry with the best tools that journalism allows.

IndieWire values in-person collaboration and team cohesion, employees work onsite 4 days a week and 1 day remotely with a focus on maintaining a vibrant and inclusive culture.

Key Responsibilities

  • Cover independent filmmakers, actors, craftspeople, and indie distributors, as well as major studios and media companies, with range, authority, and IndieWire's signature voice
  • Monitor the daily news cycle and move quickly on breaking stories, developing fresh angles and bounce pieces on the biggest stories of the day
  • Generate original story ideas and report original, sharp, and distinct stories — from breaking news to enterprise features, profiles, and analysis
  • Write compelling profiles of filmmakers, talent, and industry figures that go beyond the surface
  • Contribute reviews and critical coverage as needed, bringing a point of view grounded in deep film knowledge
  • Develop and execute strategies for breaking news and exclusives; cultivate a strong network of sources across the industry ecosystem
  • Craft compelling web headlines and optimize stories for search, applying SEO best practices throughout the publishing process
  • Maintain an active, engaged presence on social media, regularly sharing and amplifying IndieWire's coverage
  • Collaborate with editors and teammates on both coasts to develop stories and share intelligence
  • Be willing to work outside standard business hours to cover film festivals, events, and breaking developments

Required Qualifications

  • A minimum of two years of experience writing for a news organization covering film, entertainment, or media
  • Proven ability to work at speed in a breaking-news environment while maintaining accuracy and editorial standards
  • Strong writing skills across news, features, profiles, and analysis — with a clear, confident voice
  • Demonstrated experience covering film, independent cinema, or the broader media landscape
  • Fluency in SEO best practices and the ability to craft headlines optimized for web audiences
  • Active and savvy presence on social media platforms relevant to entertainment journalism
  • Self-starter with the ability to generate original ideas and develop source networks independently

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience writing film reviews and critical analysis
  • Existing relationships with publicists, agents, filmmakers, and studio or distributor contacts
  • Familiarity with digital analytics tools and how traffic data informs editorial strategy
  • Experience covering film festivals (Sundance, Cannes, TIFF, SXSW, etc.)
  • Knowledge of the indie distribution landscape and how streaming has reshaped film economics

A good faith estimate of the salary range is $70,500 - $75,000 upon hire. Factors that could be used to determine your actual salary may include your specific skills, years of experience and comparison to current employees already in this role. If you have more or less experience than specified on this job posting, please apply and list your salary expectations.

If hired, employee will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors).

It’s all About You…

PMC's comprehensive benefits package is thoughtfully designed to support every aspect of your life, empowering you to thrive both personally and professionally. We offer PMC-Paid Healthcare with no employee paycheck contributions on medical, dental, and vision for you and your family. PMC also offers Flexible Spending Accounts (Healthcare, Dependent Care & Commuter), an Employee Assistance Program, Life Insurance, Short- & Long-Term Disability, Paid Parental Leave, and a 401(k) Retirement Plan with an Employer match. Employees are also eligible to take advantage of company discounts and perks including Pet Insurance, Home & Auto Insurance, Mortgage discounts, and a variety of other savings on wellness, lifestyle, and financial essentials. As part of PMC's dedication to consistently meeting employees’ needs, we have launched a new Flexible Vacation Policy.

At PMC, we believe working in a highly collaborative, office-first environment fosters real-time communication, spontaneous idea sharing, and stronger interpersonal relationships that drive innovation and team cohesion. PMC prioritizes in-person collaboration and does not offer remote-only roles.

About IndieWire:

For over 30 years, IndieWire has been covering the business and art of entertainment. With the respect of film and TV creators, executives, and passionate fans alike, IndieWire is known for being ahead of the curve with a unique editorial voice that combines in-depth industry reporting and analysis, breaking news, and its best-in-class Oscars, Emmys, and crafts coverage. IndieWire began in July 1996 as an online chat room and evolved to become one of the earliest online entertainment news outlets. As IndieWire grew, its coverage expanded beyond film festivals and the independent film industry to include all aspects of Hollywood and the expanding universes of TV and streaming and has continued to do so since being acquired by Penske Media Corp. in 2016.

About Penske Media Corporation (PMC)

Penske Media Corporation (PMC) is a leading global media and information services company whose award-winning content attracts a passionate monthly audience of more than 500 million people. Since 2004, PMC has been a pioneer in digital media and owns over 300 live events, while reaching audiences across all screens. Penske Media is recognized, as one of the Top 100 Private Companies in the United States and North America.

Our Companies & Brands

  • Iconic Media Brands (PMX): Variety, Rolling Stone, The Verge, Billboard, The Hollywood Reporter, WWD, SHE Media, Robb Report, Deadline, Eater, Sportico, ARTnews, Fairchild Media, VIBE, IndieWire, SB Nation, ARTFORUM, POPSUGAR, Gold Derby, BEAUTY INC, Art in America, Punch, The Dodo, and more.
  • Live Events & Experiences: The Golden Globes, SXSW, Academy of Country Music Awards (ACMs), Billboard Music Awards (BBMAs), Dick Clark's New Year’s Rockin’ Eve, SXSW London, American Music Awards (AMAs), and Latin Music Week.
  • Data & Analytics: Luminate, the premier music and entertainment data and analytics company.

Global Footprint

PMC and its subsidiaries are co-headquartered in New York and Los Angeles, with additional offices spanning 14 countries worldwide.

Want to learn more? Visit www.PMC.com to explore our complete portfolio.

title: Development Engineer
description:
Electric Hydrogen’s mission is to decarbonize our world! Our outstanding people deliver creative decarbonization energy solutions to our customers.

We are seeking a Development Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will support the development of both large-scale industrial low-carbon hydrogen fuel cell power and green hydrogen e-Fuel projects. You will be responsible for leading the technical development of these projects, coordinating closely with the project development team, our internal technology and project execution groups, and external technical resources.

This position is ideal for an engineering professional with hands-on technical experience in complex industrial energy projects, particularly natural gas infrastructure, green and blue hydrogen, carbon capture and sequestration or utilization, industrial gases, low-carbon fuels, and related decarbonization pathways. The ideal candidate should be passionate about industrial decarbonization and have technoeconomic and commercial sense, polished external communication skills, project management skills, and thrive in fast-moving, uncertain environments common in project development.

You will work in a hybrid capacity from our Houston, TX office and report to the Vice President, Development.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Lead day-to-day technical activities in support of our green hydrogen, blue hydrogen, e-Fuel, and other low-carbon industrial projects, from initial concept definition through Final Investment Decision (FID).
  • Serve as the development group’s primary interface with internal and external technology, engineering, construction, and project execution groups.
  • Prepare key project deliverables such as plot plans, execution schedules, capital and operating cost estimates, plant performance and utility consumption estimates, carbon intensity / GREET modeling, inputs into financial technoeconomic models and decisionmaking, etc.
  • Lead preparation of technical aspects of external documents such as grid interconnection applications, air emissions permit applications, water source requests, natural gas supply requests, etc.
  • Support customer and commercial counterparty engagement activities, including development of proposals, project concepts, commercial discussion materials, and due diligence packages.
  • Manage external technical resources such as engineering firms.
  • Along with our internal engineering and execution teams, develop project-specific execution plans including technology selection, FEED, pre-FID equipment procurement, and EPC contractor / construction plans.
  • Monitor technology and technical market developments that impact our project developments.
  • Work with our project developers to conduct project due diligence, including evaluation of sites, infrastructure availability, permitting pathways, natural gas and CO2 infrastructure, market conditions, and potential project partners.
  • Support project financing and lender diligence activities by coordinating project information requests and technical documentation.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of engineering and project development experience within the energy, natural gas, industrial, infrastructure, hydrogen, carbon capture, renewable fuels, or clean technology sectors.
  • Experience in design and development of natural gas, blue hydrogen, carbon capture and sequestration, industrial gases, energy infrastructure, renewable fuels, or other low-carbon industrial projects through key project milestones.
  • Demonstrated understanding of project development processes, including permitting, site selection, utility coordination, natural gas supply or infrastructure diligence, CO2 transportation and sequestration considerations, commercial contracting, and stakeholder management.
  • Familiarity with carbon intensity, emissions accounting, carbon capture performance, CO2 storage or offtake pathways, and related regulatory or incentive frameworks is strongly preferred.
  • Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple parallel workstreams and competing priorities.
  • Experience working across multidisciplinary teams including engineering, environmental, commercial, legal, finance, policy, supply chain, and operations functions.
  • Strong analytical capabilities, including experience with project economics, budgeting, financial analysis, and development risk assessment.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex project issues into clear recommendations and action plans, and to represent our project design to external stakeholders.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.
  • Commitment to collaboration, integrity, inclusion, and team success.

Electric Hydrogen is a team of the world's experts in scaling technologies for the post-carbon world, with a proven record in transforming the grid and transportation sectors. Backed by some of the world's top venture capital firms, we design and manufacture electrolytic hydrogen systems matched to renewable power sources to create green hydrogen by splitting water. title: Allied Health Professional (504796L5)
description:
The Team

The Adult Mental Health Services North – Continuing Care Team (AMHS N CCT), Launceston is a multidisciplinary community mental health service within the Tasmanian Department of Health. The team provides coordinated, recovery-oriented assessment, treatment and ongoing case management for adults experiencing complex and enduring mental health conditions who require continued specialist community mental health support.

Based at 62–64 Canning Street, Launceston, the CCT works collaboratively with consumers, families and carers, General Practitioners, inpatient mental health services, the Crisis Assessment and Treatment Team, allied health professionals, community organisations, NDIS providers and other government and non-government services to promote continuity of care and support people to remain well and connected within their community.

The multidisciplinary team includes social workers, nurses, occupational therapists, psychologists, Family Carer’s support, Peers Support workforce, medical officers, psychiatrists and other clinical and support professionals. Team members work collaboratively through regular multidisciplinary review, shared care planning, clinical consultation and coordinated case management.

The service has a strong focus on:

  • comprehensive mental health assessment and ongoing clinical review;
  • recovery-oriented and person-centred care planning;
  • psychosocial and functional assessment;
  • risk assessment, monitoring and relapse prevention;
  • medication and physical-health monitoring in partnership with medical practitioners;
  • therapeutic interventions and psychoeducation;
  • family and carer engagement;
  • coordination with inpatient, primary care and community services;
  • supporting safe transitions between hospital and community care; and
  • promoting independence, social participation and long-term recovery.

AMHS N CCT is committed to delivering safe, compassionate and evidence-informed care in accordance with the Department of Health values of Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence. The team works together to ensure consumers receive coordinated, responsive and appropriate care while supporting positive outcomes for individuals, families and the broader Northern Tasmanian community.

Statewide Mental Health Services | Tasmanian Department of Health

The Role

In this role, you will provide specialist mental health assessment, evidence-based interventions and recovery-focused care to people experiencing significant and complex mental health challenges. You will manage a clinical caseload, working collaboratively with consumers, families and carers to develop treatment and recovery plans that reflect individual needs and goals.
You will work closely with colleagues across a multidisciplinary team, bringing your allied health expertise to clinical decision-making, care planning and continuity of care.

The role offers opportunities to apply and further develop your skills in therapeutic interventions, trauma-informed practice and specialised treatment approaches. You will build strong partnerships with GPs, health services, community providers and other agencies to support coordinated and effective care. As an experienced clinician, you will also contribute to clinical consultation, supervision and the development of students and less experienced staff.

You will be encouraged to grow professionally through clinical supervision, peer review and ongoing professional development, while contributing to quality and service improvement initiatives. This is an opportunity to use your clinical expertise in a role where collaboration, professional growth and making a meaningful difference in people’s recovery are central to your everyday work.

You will need

  • A minimum of two years’ post-graduate clinical experience in an area relevant to mental health service delivery, with demonstrated knowledge and skills in mental health assessment.
  • Demonstrated expertise in delivering a range of evidence-based therapeutic interventions for people experiencing significant and complex mental health problems.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide recovery-focused case management and trauma-informed care, working collaboratively with consumers, families and carers.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team and provide clinical consultation and support.
  • Demonstrated experience in liaison and consultation with GPs, health services, community providers and other agencies to support coordinated care and continuity of service.

Note: - Please refer to the Statement of Duties for all the selection criteria of this position to address in your application.

Why Tasmania

The Department of Health Tasmania oversees various hospitals across the state, including the Royal Hobart Hospital, Launceston General Hospital, Northwest Regional Hospital, and Mersey Community Hospital, as well as district hospitals and ambulance services. Additionally, it provides community health, mental health, and primary healthcare services to the Tasmanian community through more than 300 sites.

Tasmania, Australia's only island state, offers unparalleled natural beauty and a luxurious lifestyle. Pursuing your health career in Tasmania’s public health system means building strong connections with colleagues and patients. It also means embracing a lifestyle where you can enjoy extraordinary experiences outside of work while making a significant impact on the community during work.

Details of appointment

Fixed term part time, day worker position, working 64 hours per fortnight, commencing as soon as possible for a period of 12 months.

*Notwithstanding hours to be negotiated with the successful applicant.

Applicants should note that, for a period of twelve months from the date of publication, this selection process may be used to fill subsequent or similar full time, part time, and casual vacancies.

$117272 to $126182 per annum (Pro rata). Our Employer 12% superannuation contribution is on top of this amount.

Salary Packaging
