title: Technical Writer
description:
Primary Function of Position

As a member of the Services organization’s technical writing team, you’ll serve as both an independent contributor and leader in the development, delivery, and maintenance of Field Service documentation. This role combines hands-on technical writing with responsibility for establishing documentation standards, mentoring junior writers and contractors, and driving continuous improvement in documentation processes and quality.

To be successful in this role, applicants must demonstrate independence in extracting and synthesizing complex technical information from systems, subject matter experts, field demonstrations, and laboratory environments. Strong technical judgment, combined with exceptional communication skills, enables this role to evolve with changing business needs while ensuring documentation remains accurate, clear, and usable, while staying compliant with company guidelines.

This is an on-campus position with a minimum of 3 days a week in office and laboratory environments. Hands-on lab access is essential to this role’s effectiveness.

Essential Job Duties

  • Plans, writes, edits, and maintains Field Service documentation (i.e., Field Service procedures) for medical device systems with strong independent technical judgment.
  • Independently investigates and extracts technical requirements through systems review, laboratory demonstrations, engineering consultation, and field observation. Takes ownership of information gathering rather than relying on engineers to provide pre-written content.
  • Establishes and maintains documentation standards, style guidelines, templates, and best practices. Develops and refines processes to improve team productivity and quality.
  • Mentors and coaches junior writers and contractors. Provides technical feedback, reviews documentation, and contributes to team member development.
  • Completes documentation control steps to release final documentation, tracking work in JIRA and maintaining Change Order records.
  • Collaborates across product, engineering, training, and field service teams to ensure documentation meets end-to-end needs and aligns with company goals and quality standards.
  • Evaluates and recommends process improvements, tooling enhancements, and workflow optimizations. Leads or participates in documentation infrastructure initiatives.
  • Builds and maintains technical knowledge of Intuitive Surgical hardware systems sufficient to translate complex engineering concepts for field audiences.

Required Skills and Experience

  • 5+ years technical writing experience for complex hardware and medical device products (installation, maintenance, troubleshooting, repair).
  • Demonstrated ability to independently learn and understand mechanical systems through direct investigation and lab/field demonstrations.
  • Expertise in minimalist hardware documentation using DITA XML tools (Oxygen XML Editor or equivalent).
  • Professional writing samples must demonstrate technical depth, minimalist principles, and clear communication of complex concepts.
  • Exceptional writing and analytical skills; ability to grasp, validate, and effectively communicate complex scientific and engineering concepts with technical rigor.
  • Solid project-management skills; ability to manage multiple projects under tight deadlines and mentor others in project execution.
  • Proficiency with current Adobe tools (Acrobat, Illustrator, InDesign, Photoshop) for documentation graphics.
  • Medical device industry experience required. Field service or customer-facing documentation experience strongly preferred.

title: Social Skills Facilitator
description:
Position Title: Friendship Circle Facilitator
Program/Dept: Friendship Circle
Reports to: Program Manager
Classification: Regular, Part-Time, Non-Exempt

About Us: Caminar is a leading behavioral health organization that supports youth and adults across multiple counties in Northern California and the San Francisco Bay Area. Caminar builds strength and stability through comprehensive mental health and substance use treatment and wrap-around services, delivered through evidence-based, whole-person care. Founded in 1964, Caminar's vision is to be a beacon of safety, compassion, and fulfillment, supporting all those in our communities who need it most. Our mission is to build strength and stability through comprehensive mental health and substance use treatment delivered through evidence-based, whole-person care.

Caminar values diversity. People of all races, ethnicities, countries of origin, faiths, abilities, sexual orientations, and gender identities are welcome here. To learn more, please visit www.caminar.org.

Program Description: Friendship circle is a Social Integration program designed to assist adults with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities learn social skills and develop friendships. Each month we plan fun activities the participants can sign up to attend. These may include activities such as bowling, movies, walks in the park, going out to eat, playing games, community events, etc. Among other duties, the facilitators, in a company vehicle and/or their own vehicle, pick up participants who need transportation and take them to the activity. The facilitators then participate in the activity with the participants. After the activity is over the facilitator will take the participants who need transportation home. Other job duties are described below.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

  • As Facilitator, at circles you will be assisting participants with improving their social skills. Outside of circle activities, you will meet one-on-one monthly with a few individuals to update releases and assist them with discovering what they hope to achieve by participating in circles.
  • Provide support to consumers by assisting in the development and implementation of all individual service plans (ISPs). Meet as required with direct supervisor to ensure successful implementation of ISPs, use of appropriate instructional methods, and coordination of services with other involved providers and family members.
  • Assist with and instruct interpersonal and socialization skill development and recreational activities.
  • Assist consumers in connecting with and maintaining relationships in order to more actively participate in their communities.
  • Develop and maintain a respectful, caring, tolerant, ethical and empowering relationship with all individuals served while maintaining professional boundaries.
  • Maintain a minimum of 75% of total time worked in the provision of identified billable/direct services.
  • Document activities of consumers served; complete and submit all required documentation in a timely manner.
  • Attend and participate in all team meeting as scheduled and share information regarding all important interventions.
  • Report any “at risk,” unusual, or illegal activity to supervisor and/or management in a timely manner.
  • Drive personal or agency vehicle; document and report mileage according to agency procedures; comply with agency vehicle/driver policies and procedures at all times.
  • Attend all required in-person curriculum as assigned.
  • Participate in promoting a safe, healthy and clean working environment at all times consistent with applicable laws, industry standards and the agency’s own Health & Safety Program.
  • Complete and submit accurate electronic time sheets and absence reports to program management in a timely manner.
  • Promote within the agency and with the general public the philosophy and practice of social rehabilitation.
  • Actively nurture and advance the cooperative, harmonious, and teamwork-oriented environment Caminar strives to promote within the workplace through daily efforts and presentation.
  • Promote an atmosphere of dignity and respect in line with the organization’s mission, philosophy, policies and procedures.
  • Perform other related duties, responsibilities and special projects as assigned.

title: Project Management, Senior Executive
description:
We are seeking a highly organized and proactive Field Operations Senior Executive to support the execution and coordination of offline fieldwork activities across Indonesia. This role is responsible for managing vendor coordination, monitoring fieldwork execution, ensuring quality and timeline adherence, and supporting both APAC-commissioned and non-APAC commissioned studies within the BASES portfolio.

The position serves as the key liaison between internal project teams and fieldwork vendors, ensuring smooth operational delivery while maintaining compliance with NIQ quality standards and operational requirements. The role requires strong coordination skills, market research fieldwork experience, and working-level English proficiency. The scope is primarily focused on offline fieldwork operations and vendor management.

Key Responsibilities:

Offline Fieldwork Coordination

  • Coordinate and monitor offline fieldwork execution based on approved project specifications, questionnaires, survey links, and study materials provided by project teams.

  • Support fieldwork execution for both APAC-commissioned and non-APAC commissioned studies in Indonesia.

  • Track project progress and ensure field activities are completed according to agreed timelines and operational requirements.

  • Maintain project documentation, fieldwork records, and operational reports.

Vendor Management

  • Act as the primary operational contact for fieldwork vendors and external field partners.

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with vendors to ensure effective project execution.

  • Monitor vendor performance, delivery quality, productivity, and compliance with NIQ standards.

  • Support vendor sourcing, feasibility assessment, and costing discussions when required.

Quality & Compliance

  • Monitor fieldwork quality and adherence to project requirements.

  • Support investigations related to fieldwork quality concerns and collaborated with internal quality teams to identify root causes and corrective actions.

  • Document field incidents, project delays, and operational challenges for continuous operational review.

  • Ensure field activities comply with NIQ SOPs, quality guidelines, client requirements, and local regulations.

Stakeholder Coordination

  • Provide regular operational updates to project teams and relevant stakeholders.

  • Escalate timeline risks, vendor issues, or operational concerns in a timely manner.

  • Collaborate with local and regional teams to support successful project delivery.

  • Support knowledge sharing and operational improvements related to offline fieldwork management.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in marketing, Statistics, Business Administration, Management, Social Sciences, or a related field.

Experience

  • 2–5 years of experience in market research operations, fieldwork management, vendor coordination, or related operational roles.

  • Experience managing offline data collection projects and third-party vendors is preferred.

  • Experience in consumer insights, market research, or field operations is highly desirable.

  • Exposure to regional or multi-country projects is an advantage.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong coordination and execution capabilities.

  • Good understanding of offline fieldwork processes and vendor management.

  • Strong problem-solving and issue-resolution skills.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities.

  • Working-level English proficiency, both written and verbal.

  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and reporting tools.

  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and deadline-driven environment.

Key Success Measures

  • On-time completion of assigned fieldwork activities.

The Pediatric Surgery Physician Assistant assists, monitors, and manages the day-to-day needs of patients as requested by, in conjunction with, and under the supervision of a physician. Weekends and holidays as needed.

Responsibilities

1. Provide medical services under the supervision of a licensed physician, consistent with the PA's education, training and experience. 2. Performs and documents accurate, complete, and relevant history and physical assessments appropriate for the patient's age, gender, and clinical problem. 3. Orders, performs, and interprets laboratory tests and diagnostic studies/procedures in collaboration with physicians and consultants as appropriate. 4. Manages general medical and surgical conditions based on comprehensive knowledge of etiologies, risk factors, pathophysiology, and the indications and contraindications of pharmacologic agents and other treatment modalities. 5. Prescribes medication safely and effectively in accordance with best practices, hospital policy, and NJ regulations, providing patient education as needed. 6. Seeks opportunities to promote Hackensack Meridian Health (HMH) PA practice recognition (locally, nationally, and internationally) through conferences, publications, and presentations. 7. Provides care that is patient- and family-centered, compassionate, and effective for the promotion of health and treatment of disease. 8. Practices as a healthcare provider according to the rules and regulations of the Medical Staff and bylaws as outlined in the delineation of privileges. 9. Applies evidence-based and value-based medicine to systematically analyze and improve patient care practices and outcomes. 10. Evaluates patient/family transition of care planning, considering resource utilization, cost, quality, safety and self-management promotion for chronic conditions. 11. Demonstrates clinical expertise through advanced assessment and procedural skills pertinent to the practice specialty. 12. Translates `best practice' into clinical practice by evaluating current protocols and standards of care. 13. Provides culturally sensitive and educationally appropriate health management education to patients and families. 14. Facilitates consistent, coordinated care and clear communication among all members of the healthcare team through participation in daily interdisciplinary rounds. 15. Serves as an advocate for patients and families, identifying and addressing obstacles to care progression and escalating issues as appropriate. 16. Serves as a clinical resource for the multidisciplinary team by addressing clinical, process, and system improvement opportunities. 17. Participates in organizational and departmental meetings, committees, and workgroups as necessary. 18. Demonstrates the highest level of accountability for professional practice and adheres to ethical principles regarding patient confidentiality, informed consent, and adverse outcomes. 19. Promotes a collaborative work environment supporting the organizational mission, behavior expectations, values, and pillars. 20. title: Director of Finance
description:
Must have hospitality experience.

About The Moore

The Moore is a landmark destination in the Miami Design District, comprised of a private members club, hotel and a collection of restaurants, retail, exhibition, event and office space. Housed in the District’s circa-1922 Moore building, the reimagined, nearly 90,000-square-foot space integrates two, four-story structures located at the intersection of NE 40th Street and NE 2nd Avenue, and includes Elastika, the site-specific commission created by the late artist and architect Zaha Hadid for the inaugural Design Miami/ exhibition in 2005.

The Moore’s core programming extends throughout the building’s four floors: The first floor is anchored by a public, all-day dining concept, Torno Subito by Massimo Botturra. The second floor will house The Club at The Moore, a private members-only destination inclusive of a restaurant, multiple bars, lounges and private dining and event spaces. Located on the third floor, The Workplace at The Moore offers leasable private offices, dedicated desks and limited communal workplace access. The Hotel at The Moore is located on the building’s fourth floor and offers 15 hotel suites that are available for member and non-member bookings. Additionally, the fourth floor is home to The Gallery at The Moore, a 4,500-square foot private exhibition and event space that overlooks the building’s iconic Elastika atrium.

The redevelopment of The Moore is led by boutique hospitality firm and operator, WoodHouse. Founded by entrepreneur Brady Wood, WoodHouse creates, owns and operates experiential concepts, ranging from private clubs, restaurants and hotels to live music and entertainment venues.

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced and hands on Director of Finance to lead the financial operations of a dynamic, multi-faceted hospitality and membership organization in Miami, encompassing a hotel, restaurant, private social club, events, and workplace environment.

The Director of Finance will be responsible for overseeing the organization’s financial health, accounting operations, reporting, budgeting, forecasting, internal controls, and compliance. This position requires a highly organized, analytical, and collaborative finance professional who can work closely with hotel, restaurant, club, events, membership, and workplace teams to ensure financial accuracy and operational excellence.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and oversee all day-to-day finance and accounting functions across the hotel, restaurant, private club, events, and workplace operations.
  • Prepare accurate and timely monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements and management reports.
  • Monitor financial performance against budget and forecast and communicate significant variances to leadership.
  • Provide financial analysis and recommendations to support business and operational decisions.
  • Establish and maintain strong internal controls and financial procedures.
  • Ensure financial practices comply with company policies, accounting standards, and applicable regulations.
  • Identify opportunities to improve profitability, control costs, and increase operational efficiency.
  • Oversee accounts receivable and accounts payable processes across all business operations.
  • Generate, review, and process invoices accurately and timely.
  • Monitor outstanding balances and follow up on overdue accounts.
  • Apply payments to accounts and maintain accurate financial records.
  • Review vendor invoices, approvals, coding, and payment processes.
  • Maintain accurate vendor and customer account information.
  • Resolve billing, payment, and account discrepancies professionally and efficiently.
  • Prepare monthly accounts receivable and accounts payable reports.
  • Work closely with membership, events, restaurant, hotel, and workplace teams to ensure accurate billing and timely collections.
  • Reconcile daily revenue from all outlets and revenue streams, including hotel, club, restaurant, events, membership, and workplace operations.

title: Research Associate (Writing Focused)
description:

The Research Associate (RA) position reports directly to faculty supervisors and administrative manager in the Research Staff Services office.   • Coordinate personnel, fleet, equipment, materials, and subcontractor resources.

  • Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency, profitability, and customer satisfaction.

Safety is not a separate responsibility at NG Gilbert—it is part of how we operate.

The Superintendent is expected to actively promote a safety-first culture, conduct field observations and inspections, ensure crews receive appropriate training, and maintain compliance with OSHA, ANSI Z133, DOT, customer, and company safety requirements.

We’re looking for an experienced field leader who understands utility construction operations and knows how to balance people, production, safety, customers, and financial performance.

A successful Superintendent at NG Gilbert builds strong teams, understands the work happening in the field, keeps projects moving, develops trusted customer relationships, and takes ownership of operational results.

title: Senior Video Editor (Meta Ads)
description:

Eucalyptus is now part of Hims & Hers, the global leader in personalised health and wellness.

Euc is the company behind Juniper, one of the world's largest weight-management programs combining GLP-1 medication with personalised nutrition, movement support, and clinician-led care from prescribers, nurses, health coaches, pharmacists, and dietitians. About the role (What you'll be doing)

  • Edit and oversee high-volume performance content, with a strong focus on Meta-first creative

Nice to have

  • Motion graphics or animation skills
  • Experience editing for YouTube, organic social, or broader brand campaigns
  • Formal people management experience
  • Experience working in health, wellness, or another sensitive consumer category

Why join Eucalyptus?

Euc is also behind a growing family of digital healthcare clinics (Pilot, Kin, Software, Compound) across men’s health and well-being, fertility, skincare, and preventative health.

Here’s what makes joining Euc unique:

  • What’s next - Our goal for the next three years is to support 1 million patients globally to live better for longer. We’re launching into new conditions, demographics, and geographies as we build a truly preventive healthcare ecosystem.
  • Build something world-changing - We’re on the path to becoming the world’s largest international digital healthcare company. It will be challenging, fast-paced, and deeply rewarding.

title: Senior Project Manager
description:
The Project Manager – Network is responsible for the end-to-end delivery of network infrastructure projects across campus, including LAN/WAN, wireless, structured cabling, and data center connectivity work. This role leads project execution for a defined set of Network Services initiatives, coordinating closely with engineering, security, vendors, and campus stakeholders to ensure that projects are delivered on scope, on schedule, and within budget.

This position ensures that network-related projects and initiatives are well-managed, clearly documented, and operationally sound. The Project Manager partners closely with Network Engineering leadership, service owners, campus IT partners, and vendors to translate project requirements into executable plans, track delivery, manage risk, and support consistent, repeatable project practices.

This role is primarily execution-focused, providing structure, coordination, and day-to-day project management rigor that allows technical leads and service owners to focus on design, architecture, and long-term strategy.

Service Context

Project Management – Network Infrastructure

  • Manage a portfolio of network infrastructure projects and maintain visibility into:
  • Project status and milestones across planning, design, implementation, and turnover.
  • Dependencies between network projects and related Voice, OT, security, and facilities work.
  • Risks related to budget, schedule, vendor lead times, and site or access constraints.
  • Resource and capacity constraints across internal engineering teams and vendor/contractor partners.

Support consistent project practices by:

  • Preparing project status reporting tailored to network and infrastructure stakeholders.
  • Tracking decisions, design changes, and follow-ups that affect project scope, cost, and schedule.
  • Escalating risks and issues appropriately to service owners and engineering leadership.
  • Helping ensure network initiatives deliver against agreed scope, timeline, budget, and outcomes.

Operational Discipline & Process Improvement

  • Support consistent operational practices for network project delivery.
  • Assist in developing, maintaining, and operationalizing standard project processes, playbooks, and checklists for network infrastructure work, from intake through turnover.
  • Maintain documentation and reporting standards to ensure traceability of design decisions, changes, and as-built network information.
  • Participate in post-project and post-incident reviews, helping track follow-up actions and improvements across future projects.
  • Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, clarity, and coordination among engineering, vendors, and project stakeholders.

Stakeholder Coordination & Communication

  • Serve as a primary coordination point between network engineering, vendors, service owners, and project stakeholders.
  • Coordinate closely with network engineering, security, facilities, and vendor teams to align project plans and schedules.
  • Coordinate procurement, installation, testing, and cutover activities with project milestones.
  • Support preparation of materials for leadership updates, project reviews, and stakeholder communications.
  • Help ensure information flows clearly and consistently across engineering, vendor, and stakeholder teams.
  • Build effective working relationships with peers across Infrastructure, HUIT, and external vendor partners.

Business Operations & Financial Support

  • Support project stakeholders in maintaining well-managed business operations for network projects, including:
  • Budget tracking and reporting for assigned network infrastructure projects.
  • Cost transparency that clearly connects scope decisions to budget impacts.
  • Partnering with engineering leads and finance to document assumptions, trade-offs, and funding decisions.
  • Supporting vendor and contract administration, including tracking renewal dates, change orders, and vendor performance.

Ownership – Network Project Delivery

  • Serve as a primary point of contact for status, risks, and issues on assigned network infrastructure projects.
  • Maintain a clear project plan and delivery schedule for assigned initiatives, ensuring outcomes meet expectations for availability, performance, security, and usability.
  • Ensure network requirements are represented in broader project planning discussions so that scope, sequencing, and resourcing are appropriately managed.

Service Delivery and Performance Management

  • Define and maintain clear project and service definitions for assigned network work, including scope, ownership, dependencies, and escalation paths.
  • Establish and monitor schedule and risk indicators for network projects (e.g., design completion milestones, procurement lead times, site readiness, cutover windows).
  • Use project data to drive prioritization, highlight project risk, and communicate transparently with leadership, engineering, and stakeholders.
  • Manage and balance discretionary (new build/upgrade) and operational workloads (moves/adds/changes, incident or ticket resolution tied to project activities).

Security, Process Compliance, and Risk Coordination

  • Help maintain clear security, compliance, and risk management practices for network infrastructure delivered through assigned projects.
  • Partner closely with Information Security and related teams to implement appropriate controls and align projects with identity, access, and broader security strategies.
  • Ensure compliance controls are operationally feasible for project teams, auditable, and clearly communicated to stakeholders and vendors.
  • Surface and help manage trade-offs between usability, security, cost, and compliance in design and implementation decisions.

Vendor Coordination and Fiscal Support

  • Support ongoing coordination of vendor relationships tied to assigned network projects (cabling vendors, network integrators, equipment suppliers).
  • Provide input to contract renewals, scopes of work, and vendor evaluations in collaboration with HUIT VMO and Procurement.
  • Contribute to budget planning and cost tracking for assigned projects in partnership with finance and engineering leads.

User Experience, Adoption, and Change Management

  • Coordinate and manage user-visible changes resulting from network projects (e.g., network re-cuts, wireless upgrades, cutovers), balancing innovation with stability.
  • Ensure major changes are well-coordinated with schools, departments, and distributed IT, clearly communicated, and supported with appropriate documentation and cutover support.
  • Reduce friction between central services and distributed IT organizations by setting clear expectations and integrating feedback into project planning.

Cross-Functional & Enterprise Partnership

Partner closely with:

  • Information Security and Data Privacy teams for the secure design and deployment of network solutions.
  • Identity & Access Management for alignment of access and provisioning with new and updated network environments.
  • Platform and Infrastructure Services for hosting, automation, monitoring, and operational dependencies associated with network projects.
  • Schools and distributed IT leaders across a federated environment to ensure network projects support local needs while aligning with enterprise standards.

Basic Qualifications:

Basic Qualifications are the minimum threshold a candidate must meet in order to be considered for this role.

  • Minimum of five years’ progressive project management experience, including experience with IT or network infrastructure projects post-secondary education or relevant work experience

Additional Qualifications:

The following qualifications are strongly preferred. If you meet some, but not all, you are still encouraged to apply; we value employees with a willingness to learn.

  • Proven ability to manage project budgets, schedules, vendors, and resources across multiple concurrent projects.
  • Working knowledge of networking concepts (LAN/WAN, wireless, structured cabling, data center connectivity).
  • Strong knowledge of ITIL or equivalent service management frameworks.
  • Experience developing and reporting on project status, schedules, and budgets for technical stakeholders.
  • Exceptional communication, stakeholder engagement, and coordination skills with the ability to work across diverse technical and non-technical groups.
  • Experience in higher education IT environments strongly preferred.

Certifications:

  • PMP certification or equivalent project management credential preferred.
  • Completion of Harvard IT Academy Project Management Foundations course (or external equivalent) preferred
  • Working Conditions: Onsite work is performed in an office setting.
  • Hybrid: Onsite as needed with advance notice.

title: Research Assistant
description:
Job Summary

APRI - African Policy Research Institute is recruiting a Research Assistant to support policy research on climate change, inclusive development, and equitable public policy. The successful candidate will contribute to research examining how climate change and development policies affect vulnerable and historically underserved populations, with particular attention to the social, economic, governance, and public health dimensions of climate impacts.

The role will also support research exploring barriers to social inclusion experienced by persons with disabilities, and how evidence-based policy can strengthen equitable access to opportunities, services, and participation in society. Working within APRI's Climate Transition Programme, the Research Assistant will contribute to generating policy-relevant evidence that supports more inclusive, responsive, and data-driven policymaking.

Key Responsibilities
Support policy research on climate change, inclusive development, and social inclusion.
Conduct background research and policy analysis on topics related to climate resilience, equity, and vulnerable populations.
Assist in researching the socio-economic, governance, and public policy challenges affecting persons with disabilities, including persons with albinism, and identify opportunities for more inclusive policy responses.
Support the collection, organisation, cleaning, and analysis of qualitative and quantitative data to inform research outputs.
Contribute to the compilation and analysis of disaggregated data and evidence to strengthen the representation of marginalized populations in policy research.
Assist in drafting policy briefs, research reports, presentations, and other knowledge products.
Support stakeholder mapping, interviews, consultations, workshops, and other research engagements.
Monitor policy developments and emerging research on climate policy, social inclusion, disability inclusion, and sustainable development.
Support project coordination activities, including documentation, meeting notes, and tracking research outputs and deliverables.
Perform other research and programme support duties as assigned.

title: Technical Product Manager, Developer Experience (SDK)
description:
About Ping Identity:

At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it.

Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear.

While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture. We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work.

We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management.

As the Product Manager for Developer Experience, you will be the champion for the developers building on top of Ping’s Identity and Access Management (IAM) platform. Your mission is to abstract the complexities of identity standards into a seamless, secure, and intuitive developer experience across web and mobile platforms. You will bridge the gap between deep identity architecture and elegant code, ensuring that "Time to First Integration" is as fast and frictionless as possible.

In this role, you will pioneer both human and agent-first engineering for identity. You will ensure our SDKs, APIs, and tooling are optimized not just for human engineers, but for autonomous AI agents and code assistants executing end-to-end integration workflows. You will bridge the gap between deep identity architecture and elegant code, ensuring that "Time to First Integration" is fast and frictionless.

What You'll Do:

  • Drive Developer Adoption: Own the product strategy and roadmap for Ping’s Orchestration SDK across Web, iOS, Android, and Hybrid frameworks, turning complex IAM capabilities into highly adoptable developer tools.
  • Champion Developer Experience (DX): Partner with the technical documentation and developer relations teams to deliver world-class documentation, quick-start guides, and sample apps that developers love to use.
  • Cross-Functional Orchestration: Work closely with core Engineering and PM teams across the organization to ensure the SDK seamlessly exposes new identity capabilities and aligns with broader platform releases.
  • Gather Developer Insights: Actively engage with customers, partner engineers, and the open-source community to gather technical requirements, map developer journeys, and translate feedback into a prioritized backlog.
  • Evangelize the Product: Write technical blog posts, participate in developer forums, and create content that highlights SDK capabilities and modern integration patterns.
  • Execute the Vision: Manage the product lifecycle from concept to release, maintaining a well-groomed backlog, defining clear success metrics (e.g., SDK adoption, integration time), and ruthlessly prioritizing high-impact work.
  • Stay Ahead of the Curve: Continuously monitor evolving app development trends (e.g., Swift/Kotlin updates, cross-platform frameworks like Flutter/React Native) and next-generation identity standards to keep Ping’s SDK cutting-edge.
  • Incorporate AI-Focused Mindset: Seek to make mobile and web app integration more effective by staying ahead on AI-related trends (e.g., Agent Skills) as well as broader developer experience how that relates to agents and developers.
  • Contribute to wider developer-experience: Constantly assess how to improve Ping’s developer-experience holistically, contributing to wider forums and championing original ideas.

title: Senior Project Manager - Advanced Manufacturing
description:
Overview

The Senior Project Manager - Advanced Manufacturing is responsible for all project administration including all contractual requirements, agreements with trade partners, purchase orders, and risk management. This individual also manages general work performance and quality, and overall team progress against the project plan.

Suffolk is seeking people who are bold. Curious. Innovative. Caring. Looking for the career opportunity of a lifetime. We’ll challenge and inspire you to be your very best. We’ll embrace what makes you unique and lift you up as you take chances. Here, you’ll find a place where you can act with purpose and integrity, bringing intelligence and grit to every aspect of your job. Join us for the chance to achieve your ambitions and build your legacy.

Responsibilities

  • Budget Updates:
    • Produce thorough forecast of Cost-to-Complete which drills down to identify potential exposures
    • Coordinate the use of Oracle with Expedition to readily identify exposures
    • Require the project team to track costs of field directives and back charges for forecasting purposes
    • Create detailed analysis of line-item exposures, particularly unit price contracts
    • Follow the Forecasting Calendar for on-time completion of forecasts
    • Teach the Standard Operating Procedures for budget updating to others
  • Change Order Management:
    • Require the project team to fully utilize Expedition to track all Proposed Change Order (PCO) items including in-scope and out-of-scope
    • Provide the Owner with up-to-date status reports relating to Changes
    • Require the project team to produce a monthly Owner Change Order (OCO) to prevent aging of PCO issues which further allows for timely closure of Changes with Subcontractors
    • Work to recover all legitimate GC costs relating to Owner Changes
    • Track the status of all Contract Allowances in Expedition and submits Change Order Requests (COR) when an over-run is likely
    • Require the project team to track all field directives and back charges in Expedition for timely processing on a monthly basis, i.e. composite clean-up, hoisting time, etc.
  • Project Close Out:
    • Establish an effective Close-out Plan early in the project which includes the early collection, review, and packaging of Contract close-out documents
    • Implement the use of the Noncompliance Reporting System
    • Require the team to utilize the Work list System to organize and manage the completion of phases of the work
    • Utilize the Completion-Compliance-Quality Form (CCQ) process for close-out
    • Teach close out process to other SCCI employees
  • Owner/Sub Requisition Process:
    • Require the project team to have the completed pay requisitions approved by the Owner no later than the 1st of each month
    • Produce an effective Schedule of Values
    • Establish a regimented process for the collection of payments no later than 30 days and subsequent efficient system for the payment to Subcontractors
    • Review the Hold Reports before payment is due to allow for timely handling of deficiency issues and payment to Subcontractors/Vendors
  • Cash Management:
    • Consistently manage the cash flow of the Project to maintain a fiscally responsible position for SCCI
    • Produce an effective Schedule of Values which supports a strong cash flow position
    • Review each Subcontractors initial Schedule of Values to prevent overpayment
    • Review Sub/Vendor requisitions to prevent payment of unsigned or unfunded Change Orders
    • Produce and update the cash model for the Owner to prevent surprises
    • Produce an accurate percent complete projection to support the SCCI financial management process
  • Meeting Management:
    • Establishes a meeting regiment for the Project Team which provides for effective communication and problem solving
    • Follow the SOP for focused meetings such as PM/PE, OAC's, subcontractor meetings, coordination meetings, Precon Sessions, etc.
    • Manage all meetings by agenda and work to time limits
  • Contract Logs:
    • Require the Project Team to assemble and maintain the Project Logs (Cash Management, Change Management, Noncompliance, Buy-Schedule, Contracts, Procurement, Submittals, RFI's, Safety, Hold Reports, Construction Schedule, Work lists) and periodically review for accuracy
    • Conduct focus meetings once per month to review the maintenance of those logs and drills down to identify potential exposures and issues
  • Subcontractor Relationships:
    • Establish a "Firm but Fair" approach to building relationships with Subcontractors
    • Promote an environment of organization and professionalism with Subcontractors
    • Address issues immediately with a non-performing Subcontractor to protect SCCI from resulting delay and potential impact
  • Exhibit B Purchasing Process:
    • Work with the Project Team, including Superintendents and Estimators, to consistently produce clear, thorough, and accurate Scopes of Work based on drilled down review of documents
    • Organize and administer a well-planned purchasing process to prevent the "Just in time" purchase of materials
    • Understand the priority of timely buy-out and gather the resources to meet the buy schedule
  • Schedule Management:
    • Provide leadership with the Superintendent to produce a clear, thorough, and accurate baseline Contract Schedule which rarely requires changes to the original logic
    • Track events, impacts, and changes in the schedule to allow for the management and prevention of delays
    • Lead the Project Team to focus on critical path matters to prevent non-excusable delays
    • Manage and distribute organized and efficient Monthly Updating Process in accordance with the SCCI SOP
    • Provide the Owner with written monthly updates of the Contract Schedule in accordance with the requirements of the Contract
    • Take decisive action with subcontractors that are impacting the schedule
    • Produce buy-out and procurement schedule and assist with writing monthly schedule narrative in conjunction with the Scheduling team
  • Risk Management:
    • Complete the buy-out process in a manner which permits the timely flow of work, prevents budget issues, contract executions, bonds, insurance, etc.
    • Write timely notices to Owner and Subcontractors
    • Secure CCD authorizations before proceeding with Changes
    • Take immediate action when a non-performing Subcontractor is likely to cause impact to the Project
    • Work to complete the submittal and coordination process no later than 180 days
    • Teaches a risk management regiment to others on the project team
  • Owner Relationship:
    • Work to establish a trusting and professional relationship with the Owner
    • Focus on keeping the Owner well informed of important matters to prevent surprises
    • Work to secure a strong letter of recommendation from the Owner for SCCI
  • Quality Management:
    • Provide leadership in the utilization of the Quality Management Program on the project, which outlines quality expectations
    • Participate with the project team to institute the use of First Delivery and Quality Benchmark Inspections as the work progresses
    • Implement the use of the Nonconformance Reporting System to track and manage deficiencies in the work
    • Require the use of mock-ups to establish the quality expectations as defined in the Quality Management Program
  • Team Leadership:
    • Strive to create synergy and a teamwork atmosphere on the project
    • Lead by example by establishing the work ethic guidelines for the entire team and therefore establishes the boundaries and expectations
    • Organize periodic team events and training sessions to advance the SCCI strategy of "Train & Develop Our People
    • Act immediately when personal conflicts emerge among the team
  • Mentoring/Training:
    • Oversee career and educational development of team personnel
    • Require the adherence of standard operation procedures and actively teach each process

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in applicable discipline and a minimum of 10 years of experience within the Advanced Manufacturing space
  • Excellent business judgment demonstrated by consistently achieving profitability objectives and strong project close-outs with client and subcontractor relationships in good standing
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail evidenced by a strong command of all applicable contract and legal provisions
  • Ability to consistently analyze and execute financial trade-offs which frequently involve dealing with incomplete data and ambiguity
  • Ability to constantly multi-task and handle competing priorities between Suffolk business needs, organizational issues, and sound customer relations
  • Possess judgment to know when to appropriately escalate issues up the chain of command
  • The ability to manage and embrace change. Respond and adapt to new processes and new ways of looking at old problems
  • A strong sense of urgency and initiative. Able to quickly study and react to complex issues
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to confidently and decisively take action
  • Team leader with excellent diplomatic and communication skills, able to handle and resolve conflicts effectively in a firm but fair manner
  • Candidate must possess Suffolk’s Core Values: Passion, Integrity, Hard Work, Professionalism, and Caring

Working Conditions

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit for long periods of time; talk or hear; perform fine motor, hand and finger skills in the use of a keyboard, telephone, or writing. The employee is frequently required to stand; walk; and reach with arms and/or hands. Specific vision abilities include close vision, distance vision, depth perception and the ability to adjust focus. The employee will spend their time in an office environment with a quiet to moderate noise level. Job site walking.

title: CVP Software Infrastructure and Forward Deployed Engineering
description:
ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD.

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career.




THE ROLE:

Own the two capabilities that most directly determine how fast and how well AIG's software organization ships: (1) the engineering infrastructure and developer productivity layer that AIG's software teams run on, and (2) the Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) function that puts AMD software into customers' and partners' hands and converts field learnings back into the roadmap.

THE PERSON:

Define and institutionalize the Software Infrastructure and FDE Engagement to maximize resource leverage and ensure consistent, high-velocity customer outcomes. Serve as the Voice of the Customer internally: Translate field intelligence and customer challenges into concrete, prioritized engineering roadmaps, and ensure execution.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  1. Software Infrastructure & Developer Productivity

Own developer productivity, engineering velocity, and the internal developer platform for AIG's software organization — the tooling, CI/CD, and workflows engineers use every day.

Manage developer workloads and productivity against GPU capacity, integrating CI/CD, test, and utilization for these engineering workflows directly into the engineering organization.

Operate on a clear division of responsibility with IT: IT provides and manages the standardized base infrastructure and the underlying SLAs; engineering owns the developer-facing workloads, CI/CD pipelines, and utilization/efficiency of that capacity — with the intent that these engineering-integrated workflows are increasingly managed by engineering over time.

Establish honest, non-punitive productivity and utilization metrics that drive real efficiency gains in how AIG consumes GPU and compute capacity.

  1. Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE)

Build and lead the FDE function for AIG's software organization — engineers deployed alongside key customers and partners to deploy, integrate, and optimize AMD software (ROCm and the broader AI stack) in real workloads.

Close the loop between the field and the core engineering roadmap: translate deployment friction, performance gaps, and customer requirements into prioritized engineering work.

Serve as a scaling mechanism for adoption — turning individual high-touch engagements into repeatable patterns, reference architectures, and tooling that reduce the cost of the next deployment.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:

  • Years of Technical Leadership: Demonstrated track record leading high-impact technical teams within high-stakes environments (e.g., Cloud Infrastructure, AI Platform, or HPC).
  • The "Hardware/Software" Hybrid: You understand the stack from the metal up.
  • Commercial Acumen & Fluency: Deep understanding of commercial drivers (ARR, Churn, Margin) and the ability to articulate how technical solutions impact deal velocity and business outcomes.
  • High-Stakes Crisis Management: Experience leading through "Sev0" customer incidents (e.g., massive training run failures), demonstrating the poise and clarity required to manage executive communication while guiding rapid root cause resolution.

ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS:

  • BS, MS or equivalent with direct experience

title: AI Governance
description:
We believe in the power of ingenuity to build a positive human future. We challenge where it matters and own the outcome. We combine strategic thinking, customer-centric service design, and agile engineering practices to help organisations harness the potential of Artificial Intelligence safely, responsibly, and at scale.

Why consider joining our Digital & Data community? 🤔

  • Join our Digital & Data team working alongside AI specialists, data scientists, engineers, cyber security experts, risk professionals, regulatory specialists, and cross-disciplinary teams to help clients unlock value from AI while managing associated risks.
  • Grow a flexible and unique career within a trust-based, inclusive environment that values excellence, innovation, and curiosity. You have the option to progress with us on a technical career track. No need to go onto the Partner career track if this doesn’t align with what you want to do.
  • Hybrid working – our approach is to be in the office or on client site a minimum of 2 days per week.
  • Hybrid working - our approach is to be in the office or on client site a minimum of 2 days per week.
  • Work on a broad variety of projects and tech stacks for clients across seven sectors - no project is ever the same
  • Join other experts within our supportive and collaborative tech community through knowledge-sharing and peer-level support, coaching and mentoring
  • Deepen your expertise through our culture of learning and growth – you’ll have budget to take courses (technical and non-technical training), plus gain certifications

What you can expect 🌱

  • Work to agile best practices and cross-functionally with multiple teams and stakeholders. You'll be helping clients design, implement and operationalise AI governance frameworks, as well as contributing to internal initiatives.
  • Support clients in navigating emerging AI regulations, standards, and guidance while enabling innovation and business value.
  • Facilitate workshops, governance forums, risk assessments, and operating model design activities with senior stakeholders.
  • Live in-person whiteboarding sessions to problem solve as a team, alongside asynchronous communication on Teams.
  • Hybrid working with the team on client site or in our office a minimum of two days per week. However, the actual time you spend and where you spend it will vary by role or assignment, including up to 5 days per week on a client site.
  • An environment that deeply cares about its values Values | PA Consulting.

Essential requirements ✅

You must be an established consulting professional with experience delivering projects focused on AI governance, responsible AI, AI risk management, model governance, or emerging technology regulation within the private sector. Ideally, you should have experience consulting with Life Sciences, Government or Consumer & Manufacturing sector clients.

Even if you don’t meet every requirement below, feel free to still apply as we are often hiring for similar roles which your background might be better suited to.

  • You thrive in problem-solving and analytical thinking.
  • You enjoy collaborating with multiple stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proven experience with AI governance frameworks, policies, controls, and operating models.
  • Experience interpreting and applying AI-related regulations, standards, and guidance, such as the EU AI Act, NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF), ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 23894, OECD AI Principles, and emerging regulatory requirements.
  • Experience conducting AI risk assessments, model governance reviews, algorithmic impact assessments, or responsible AI evaluations.
  • Familiarity with AI lifecycle governance, including controls relating to model development, validation, deployment, monitoring, explainability, transparency, accountability, and human oversight.
  • Experience working with Generative AI technologies and associated governance considerations, including data usage, intellectual property, security, privacy, bias, and model risk.
  • The ability to efficiently understand client organisations and their business models and to tailor AI governance approaches to their strategic, operational, and regulatory requirements.
  • The ability to communicate effectively with different stakeholders (e.g. business, legal, compliance, risk, IT, security, data science, and engineering teams) on AI governance and responsible AI matters.
  • An analytical mindset, with a focus on producing quality work in a results-oriented environment.

Desirable qualifications and experience

  • Experience implementing governance tooling, AI inventory solutions, model risk management platforms, or GRC technologies.
  • Experience with data governance, privacy, cyber security, model risk management, or technology risk disciplines.
  • Knowledge of machine learning and Generative AI technologies, including Large Language Models (LLMs).
  • Possession of relevant certifications such as ISO 42001 Lead Implementer/Auditor, IAPP AIGP, CRISC, CISM, CISSP, AWS/Azure AI certifications, or equivalent. Where you do not have the qualifications, we will support you in achieving them.
  • Experience defining AI governance processes, committees, policies, standards, controls, and reporting frameworks.
  • Experience supporting AI governance programmes within highly regulated sectors is preferred.

Please be aware that some of our UK roles at PA Consulting require a UK security clearance.

All PA people are required to undergo background checks and to achieve the Baseline Personnel Security Standard; however, some UK roles also require higher levels of National Security Vetting, where applicants must have at least 5 years of continuous residency in the UK.

We therefore ask that you only apply if you meet the residency requirements (i.e. you are a British citizen or have been resident in the UK for the past 5 years), as this is the prerequisite for a security clearance. If you're unsure about your eligibility, we encourage you to review the UK Government’s guidance on security vetting before applying.

title: Senior Industrial Designer
description:
We are seeking a Senior Industrial Designer to translate design vision into production-ready form language for our next-generation robotic platforms. You will own form development from early volumetric exploration through surface refinement — defining what our robots look and feel like while ensuring designs are manufacturable from the start. You’ll work at the intersection of aesthetics and engineering, balancing proportion, character, and visual brand coherence with the realities of complex electromechanical packaging, dynamic articulation, and production tooling.

Key job responsibilities
- Form Development & Surface Refinement: Explore, iterate, and refine complex multi-part robotic enclosures, articulating fairings, and structural chassis using Rhino, SubD, Alias, or Blender — from rapid volumetric studies through production-intent surfacing with Class-A quality standards.
- Design for Manufacturing: Incorporate draft angles, parting line strategy, wall thickness constraints, and tooling considerations into the design process from the start. Develop surfaces with production intent across injection molding, sheet metal, die casting, and composite fabrication processes.
- Unified Design Language: Establish and maintain a cohesive visual brand language across the entire robot — ensuring seamless aesthetic and proportional transitions between static and moving components.
- Dynamic Articulation & Clearances: Explore and resolve how physical panels interact, reveal internal mechanisms, and clear dynamic ranges of motion while maintaining design intent.
- Component Packaging & Integration: Collaborate closely with mechanical engineering, robotics, and manufacturing teams to package high-density motor assemblies, cooling systems, battery modules, and sensor arrays into an appealing, functional, and producible envelope.
- Engineering Handoff: Deliver organized, proportion-locked CAD models (SubD / clean NURBS / production-intent surfaces) with clear design intent documentation — character lines, highlight priorities, parting line intent, and DFM annotations ready for tooling development.
